properties.description:
...FIRE WEATHER WATCH FOR HIGH WINDS AND ACTIVE WILDFIRES IN EFFECT

FROM SATURDAY MORNING THROUGH SATURDAY EVENING....

The National Weather Service in Elko has issued a Fire Weather
Watch, which is in effect from Friday afternoon through Friday
evening. a Fire Weather Watch has also been issued from Saturday
morning through Saturday evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire weather zones 424, 437, 438, 469, and
470.

* WIND...Sustained winds up to 15-20 mph, gusts 25-30 mph Friday
afternoon. Sustained winds up to 20-25 mph, gusts 35-40 mph
Saturday.

* HIGHEST THREAT...Highest threat will be in fire zones 437 and
469 due to active wildfires in the area along with high winds.

* IMPACTS...any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.
High winds may impact active wildfires to spread further. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:

are forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible
red flag warnings.

such as asthma, limit prolonged outdoor exertion.

Arkansas, and DeSoto County Mississippi, including the city of

exceed the Environmental Protection Agency's federal safe health
standard. The Shelby County Health Department recommends that
sensitive groups which include active children and adults, and
people with respiratory disease, such as asthma, limit prolonged
outdoor exertion.

until monitored values return to safe levels. For more information go
to www.airnow.gov.

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued October 7 at 4:10PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
HLSMOB

This product covers portions of southwest Alabama...northwest Florida...south
central Alabama...and inland southeast Mississippi.

**ISAIAS QUICKLY INTENSIFYING, FORECAST TO BE A HURRICANE BY THURSDAY
MORNING**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Watch has been issued for Butler, Clarke,
Crenshaw, George, Greene, Monroe, Washington, and Wilcox
- A Hurricane Watch has been issued for Conecuh, Covington, and
Escambia

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for Butler, Clarke,
Crenshaw, George, Greene, Monroe, Washington, and Wilcox
- A Storm Surge Watch and Hurricane Watch are in effect for
Baldwin Central, Baldwin Coastal, Escambia Coastal, Mobile
Central, Mobile Coastal, Okaloosa Coastal, and Santa Rosa
Coastal
- A Hurricane Watch is in effect for Baldwin Inland, Conecuh,
Covington, Escambia, Escambia Inland, Mobile Inland, Okaloosa
Inland, and Santa Rosa Inland

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 630 miles south-southwest of Mobile AL or about 640 miles
southwest of Pensacola FL
- 22.7N 92.9W
- Storm Intensity 65 mph
- Movement East-northeast or 65 degrees at 8 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Isaias has strengthened and should continue to
intensify through Friday morning. Isaias is currently moving east-
northeast and should eventually turn northward and accelerate
towards the north central Gulf coast. As it nears the coast, wind
fields will expand with the potential for significant wind impacts
and a life threatening storm surge along and to the east of where
the hurricane makes landfall. There still remains uncertainty with
the eventual speed and track of the hurricane so everyone should
continue to closely monitor the latest forecast over the next few
days.

Areas of heavy rainfall and flooding are possible although with the
fast speed of the hurricane at landfall we are currently expecting 3
to 7 inches with localized amounts up to 10 inches near the coast.
In addition, a favorable environment for tornadoes will also develop
to the east of the track as it moves inland Friday through Saturday.

Please continue to monitor the latest forecast updates and follow
the advise of your local emergency management officials.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* SURGE:
Prepare for life-threatening surge having possible extensive impacts
across the Alabama and western Florida panhandle coasts. Potential
impacts in this area include:
- Large areas of deep inundation with storm surge flooding
accentuated by battering waves. Structural damage to buildings,
with several washing away. Damage compounded by floating
debris. Locations may be uninhabitable for an extended period.
- Large sections of near-shore escape routes and secondary roads
washed out or severely flooded. Flood control systems and
barriers may become stressed.
- Severe beach erosion with significant dune loss.
- Major damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks, and piers. Many
small craft broken away from moorings, especially in
unprotected anchorages with some lifted onshore and stranded.

Elsewhere across portions of southwest Alabama...northwest
Florida...south central Alabama...and inland southeast Mississippi.,
little to no impact is anticipated.

* WIND:
Prepare for life-threatening wind having possible extensive impacts
across southwest and portions of south central Alabama and the western
Florida panhandle. Potential impacts in this area include:
- Considerable roof damage to sturdy buildings, with some having
window, door, and garage door failures leading to structural
damage. Mobile homes severely damaged, with some destroyed.
Damage accentuated by airborne projectiles. Locations may be
uninhabitable for weeks.
- Many large trees snapped or uprooted along with fences and
roadway signs blown over.
- Some roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban
or heavily wooded places.
- Large areas with power and communications outages.

Also, prepare for dangerous wind having possible limited to
significant impacts across portions of southeast Mississippi and the
remainder of southwest Alabama.

* TORNADOES:
Prepare for a tornado event having possible limited impacts across
coastal southwest Alabama, the western Florida panhandle, and
portions of southwest and south central Alabama. Potential impacts
include:
- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power
and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys
toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats
pulled from moorings.

Elsewhere across portions of southwest Alabama...northwest
Florida...south central Alabama...and inland southeast Mississippi.,
little to no impact is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Prepare for life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible
extensive impacts across coastal Alabama and the western Florida
panhandle. Potential impacts include:
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may
become dangerous rivers. Flood control systems and barriers may
become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.
Streets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with
underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.
Many road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.

Prepare for dangerous rainfall flooding having possible significant
impacts across interior areas of southwest and south central Alabama.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to check your emergency plan and emergency supplies
kit and take necessary actions to protect your family and secure your
home or business.

When making safety and preparedness decisions, do not focus on the
exact forecast track since hazards such as flooding rain, damaging
wind gusts, storm surge, and tornadoes extend well away from the
center of the storm.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For the latest detailed evacuation and shelter information...please
refer to your local emergency management agency at the phone number
or website listed below.
- Coastal Alabama:
- Baldwin County: 251-972-6807 or
www.baldwincountyal.gov/departments/EMA
- Mobile County: 251-460-8000 or mobilecountyema.gov
- Northwest Florida:
- Escambia County: 850-471-6400 or myescambia.com/beready
- Santa Rosa County: 850-983-5360 www.santarosa.fl.gov/emergency
- Okaloosa County: 850-651-7150 or myokaloosa.com/emergency-management
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Mobile AL around 10 PM CDT, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

HLSTAE

This product covers eastern Florida panhandle, Florida Big Bend,
southeastern Alabama and southwestern Georgia

**ISAIAS QUICKLY INTENSIFYING, FORECAST TO BE A HURRICANE BY THURSDAY
MORNING**


NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Watch has been issued for Calhoun, Coffee,
Dale, Geneva, Henry, Houston, Inland Franklin, Jackson,
Northern Liberty, and Southern Liberty

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Storm Surge Watch and Hurricane Watch are in effect for
Coastal Bay, Coastal Gulf, and South Walton
- A Storm Surge Watch and Tropical Storm Watch are in effect for
Coastal Franklin, Coastal Jefferson, and Coastal Wakulla
- A Hurricane Watch is in effect for Central Walton and North
Walton
- A Storm Surge Watch is in effect for Coastal Dixie and Coastal
Taylor
- A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for Calhoun, Coffee, Dale,
Geneva, Henry, Holmes, Houston, Inland Bay, Inland Franklin,
Inland Gulf, Jackson, Northern Liberty, Southern Liberty, and
Washington

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 680 miles southwest of Panama City or about 690 miles
southwest of Apalachicola
- 22.7N 92.9W
- Storm Intensity 65 mph
- Movement East-northeast or 65 degrees at 8 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

...TROPICAL STORM WATCH ISSUED FOR SOUTHEAST ALABAMA AND INLAND FLORIDA PANHANDLE
COUNTIES...

At 5 PM ET, Tropical Storm Isaias was still located in the Bay of
Campeche with maximum sustained winds of 65 mph and moving ENE at
8 mph. Isaias is forecast to turn northward in the next day or so and
accelerate in forward speed towards the central Gulf coast. Steady
strengthening is expected through much of the next couple of days,
although some weakening may be possible just before landfall. The wind
field is expected to expand considerably and may be lopsided towards
the east, leading to windier conditions for portions of our area.
There is still considerable uncertainty with both timing and track.
Conditions could begin to deteriorate across the Panhandle as early as
Friday morning.

Given the expected large size of Isaias, the wind threat may extend
well into the eastern portions of our area. An expected fast forward
speed may also lead to the wind threat extending further inland. Storm
surge will be possible along our whole coastline including the
Panhandle and Apalachee Bay. Inundation values of 5 to 7 feet above
ground level (AGL) are possible across the coastal Panhandle to Indian
Pass, 4 to 6 feet AGL from Indian Pass to the Steinhatchee River, and
2 to 4 feet AGL from the Steinhatchee River to Yankeetown.

Soggy conditions across the region from recent rainfall will make the
area more sensitive to flooding from additional heavy rainfall from
Isaias. Forecast rainfall totals of 3 to 7 inches is expected across
much of the area, with isolated amounts near 10 inches possible. If
realized, these values would likely cause at least isolated flash
flooding and some river flooding. It is too soon to determine exact
tornado impacts, but there is an elevated chance for tornadoes Friday
into Saturday.



POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* FLOODING RAIN:
Prepare for life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible
extensive impacts across the Florida Panhandle and portions of SE
Alabama. Potential impacts include:
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, and ditches may become
dangerous rivers. Flood control systems and barriers may become
stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.
Streets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with
underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.
Many road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.

Prepare for dangerous rainfall flooding having possible limited to
significant impacts across southeast Alabama, southwest Georgia, and
the Florida Big Bend.

* WIND:
Prepare for dangerous wind having possible significant impacts across
Southeast Alabama and the Florida Panhandle. Potential impacts in this
area include:
- Some damage to roofing and siding materials, along with damage
to porches, awnings, carports, and sheds. A few buildings
experiencing window, door, and garage door failures. Mobile
homes damaged, especially if unanchored. Unsecured lightweight
objects become dangerous projectiles.
- Several large trees snapped or uprooted, but with greater
numbers in places where trees are shallow rooted. Several
fences and roadway signs blown over.
- Some roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban
or heavily wooded places. A few bridges, causeways, and access
routes impassable.
- Scattered power and communications outages, but more prevalent
in areas with above ground lines.

Also, prepare for hazardous wind having possible limited impacts
across the Florida Big Bend and Southeast Alabama.

Elsewhere across eastern Florida panhandle, Florida Big Bend, and
southwestern Georgia, little to no impact is anticipated.

* SURGE:
Prepare for life-threatening surge having possible extensive impacts
across coastal Florida Panhandle and Florida Big Bend. Potential
impacts in this area include:
- Large areas of deep inundation with storm surge flooding
accentuated by battering waves. Structural damage to buildings,
with several washing away. Damage compounded by floating
debris. Locations may be uninhabitable for an extended period.
- Large sections of near-shore escape routes and secondary roads
washed out or severely flooded. Flood control systems and
barriers may become stressed.
- Severe beach erosion with significant dune loss.
- Major damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks, and piers. Many
small craft broken away from moorings, especially in
unprotected anchorages with some lifted onshore and stranded.

Elsewhere across eastern Florida panhandle, Florida Big Bend,
southeastern Alabama and southwestern Georgia, little to no impact is
anticipated.

* TORNADOES:
Prepare for a tornado event having possible limited impacts across the
Florida Panhandle. Potential impacts include:
- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power
and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys
toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats
pulled from moorings.

Elsewhere across eastern Florida panhandle, Florida Big Bend,
southeastern Alabama and southwestern Georgia, little to no impact is
anticipated.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to check your emergency plan and emergency supplies
kit and take necessary actions to protect your family and secure your
home or business.

When making safety and preparedness decisions, do not focus on the
exact forecast track since hazards such as flooding rain, damaging
wind gusts, storm surge, and tornadoes extend well away from the
center of the storm.


If you live in a place particularly vulnerable to flooding, such as
near the Gulf of America or a large inland lake, in a low-lying or
poor drainage area, or near an already swollen river, plan to move to
safe shelter on higher ground.

Always heed the advice of local officials and comply with orders that
are issued. Do not needlessly jeopardize your life or the lives of
others.

When securing your property, outside preparations should be concluded
as soon as possible before conditions deteriorate. The onset of
strong gusty winds or flooding can cause certain preparedness
activities to become unsafe.

Be sure to let friends and family members know of your intentions for
weathering the storm and your whereabouts. Have someone located away
from the threatened area serve as your point of contact. Share vital
contact information with others. Keep cell phones handy and charged.

Check on those who may not be fully aware of the situation or who are
unable to make personal preparations.

If you are a visitor, know the name of the county in which you are
located and where it is relative to current watches and warnings. If
staying at a hotel, ask the management staff about their onsite
disaster plan. Listen for evacuation orders, especially pertaining to
area visitors.

------------------

region into the weekend. While there is currently no concerns for
tropical storm force winds in the local area, there is the potential

-----------------

impacts across Coastal Levy County. Potential impacts in
this area include:
- Areas of inundation with storm surge flooding accentuated by
waves. Damage to several buildings, mainly near the coast.

weakened or washed out, especially in usually vulnerable low
spots.

numerous rip currents.
- Moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks, and piers.
Several small craft broken away from moorings, especially in
unprotected anchorages.

impacts across coastal Citrus, Hernando, Pasco, Pinellas and Hillsborough Counties.

impact is anticipated.

somewhere within this area within the next 48 hours

* LOCATIONS AFFECTED
- Homewood
- Monroeville

* WIND
- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Equivalent Tropical Storm force wind
- Peak Wind Forecast: 35-45 mph with gusts to 55 mph
- Window for Tropical Storm force winds: Friday evening until
early Saturday morning

UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for wind 58
to 73 mph
- The wind threat has remained nearly steady from the
previous assessment.

storm force.

underway. Prepare for significant wind damage.

becomes hazardous.

damage to porches, awnings, carports, and sheds. A few
buildings experiencing window, door, and garage door
failures. Mobile homes damaged, especially if unanchored.

numbers in places where trees are shallow rooted. Several
fences and roadway signs blown over.
- Some roads impassable from large debris, and more within
urban or heavily wooded places.
- Scattered power and communications outages, but more
prevalent in areas with above ground lines.

* FLOODING RAIN
- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST:
- Peak Rainfall Amounts: 3-6 inches, with locally higher
amounts

UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for
moderate flooding rain

the previous assessment.
- PLAN: Emergency plans should include the potential for
moderate flooding from heavy rain. Evacuations and rescues
are possible.
- PREPARE: Consider protective actions if you are in an area
vulnerable to flooding.
- ACT: Heed any flood watches and warnings. Failure to take
action may result in serious injury or loss of life.

- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Significant
- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations
and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with
swifter currents and overspill their banks in a few places,
especially in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams,
creeks, canals, and ditches overflow.
- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken
foundations. Several places may experience expanded areas
of rapid inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and
poor drainage areas. Some streets and parking lots take on
moving water as storm drains and retention ponds overflow.
Driving conditions become hazardous. Some road and bridge
closures.

* TORNADO
- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST:
- Situation is unfavorable for tornadoes

- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST
UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Tornadoes not expected

with gusty winds may still occur.
- PREPARE: Little to no preparations needed to protect
against tornadoes at this time. Keep informed of the latest
tornado situation.
- ACT: Listen for changes in the forecast.

- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Little to None
- Little to no potential impacts from tornadoes.

- ACT: Leave if evacuation orders are given for your area.

your life.

accentuated by battering waves. Structural damage to
buildings, with several washing away. Damage compounded by

roads washed out or severely flooded.

major flooding from heavy rain. Evacuations and rescues are
likely.

if you are in an area vulnerable to flooding.

action will likely result in serious injury or loss of life.

rescues.

multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches

barriers may become stressed.

washed away. Many places where flood waters may cover
escape routes. Streets and parking lots become rivers of
moving water with underpasses submerged. Driving conditions
become dangerous. Many road and bridge closures with some
weakened or washed out.

- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST:

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued October 7 at 4:02PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
HLSLIX

This product covers Southeast Louisiana and South Mississippi

...ISAIAS QUICKLY INTENSIFYING, FORECAST TO BE A HURRICANE BY THURSDAY
MORNING...

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- The Storm Surge Watch has been cancelled for Upper St. Bernard

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Storm Surge Watch and Hurricane Watch are in effect for
Southern Harrison and Southern Jackson
- A Storm Surge Watch and Tropical Storm Watch are in effect for
Eastern Orleans, Lower Plaquemines, Lower St. Bernard,
Southeast St. Tammany, and Southern Hancock
- A Hurricane Watch is in effect for Northern Harrison and
Northern Jackson

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 530 miles south-southwest of New Orleans LA or about 580
miles south-southwest of Gulfport MS
- 22.7N 92.9W
- Storm Intensity 65 mph
- Movement East-northeast or 65 degrees at 8 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Isaias is currently in the southwest Gulf and will
continue to strengthen as it moves to the east-northeast and
eventually the northeast through Friday. Tropical Storm Isaias is
forecast to bring the threat of tropical storm force wind gusts,
locally heavy rainfall, and storm surge of 3 to 5 feet to coastal
portions of southeast Louisiana from the mouth of the Mississippi
River to the Rigolets and from Bay Saint Louis westward in coastal
Mississippi. Isaias is forecast to bring the threat of hurricane force
wind gusts, locally heavy rainfall, and storm surge of 5 to 7 feet
from Bay Saint Louis eastward in coastal Mississippi. The most likely
time for impacts will be Friday into Saturday.

Storm surge watches are in effect from the mouth of the Mississippi
River to the Alabama and Mississippi state line. Hurricane watches are
in effect from Ocean Springs to the Alabama and Mississippi state
line. Tropical storm watches are in effect from the Jefferson and
Plaquemine Parish line in southeast Louisiana to Ocean Springs in
coastal Mississippi.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Prepare for life-threatening wind having possible extensive impacts
for locations east of Ocean Springs in coastal Mississippi. Potential
impacts in this area include:
- Considerable roof damage to sturdy buildings, with some having
window, door, and garage door failures leading to structural
damage. Mobile homes severely damaged, with some destroyed.
Damage accentuated by airborne projectiles. Locations may be
uninhabitable for weeks.
- Many large trees snapped or uprooted along with fences and
roadway signs blown over.
- Some roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban
or heavily wooded places. Several bridges, causeways, and
access routes impassable.
- Large areas with power and communications outages.

Also, prepare for dangerous wind having possible limited to
significant impacts for locations west of Ocean Springs in coastal
Mississippi and for extreme coastal portions of southeast Louisiana
from the mouth of the Mississippi River eastward.

* SURGE:
Prepare for life-threatening surge having possible extensive impacts
for coastal locations east of Ocean Springs in coastal Mississippi.
Potential impacts in this area include:
- Large areas of deep inundation with storm surge flooding
accentuated by battering waves. Structural damage to buildings,
with several washing away. Damage compounded by floating
debris. Locations may be uninhabitable for an extended period.
- Large sections of near-shore escape routes and secondary roads
washed out or severely flooded. Flood control systems and
barriers may become stressed.
- Severe beach erosion with significant dune loss.
- Major damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks, and piers. Many
small craft broken away from moorings, especially in
unprotected anchorages with some lifted onshore and stranded.

Also, prepare for locally hazardous surge having possible significant
impacts for coastal locations west of Ocean Springs in coastal
Mississippi and for locations outside of the hurricane risk reduction
system in southeast Louisiana from the Pearl River south to the mouth
of the Mississippi.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Prepare for dangerous rainfall flooding having possible significant
impacts for locations east of Ocean Springs in coastal Mississippi.
Potential impacts include:
- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with swifter
currents and overspill their banks in a few places, especially
in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams, creeks, canals, and
ditches overflow.
- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken foundations.
Several places may experience expanded areas of rapid
inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Some streets and parking lots take on moving water as
storm drains and retention ponds overflow. Driving conditions
become hazardous. Some road and bridge closures.

Prepare for locally hazardous rainfall flooding having possible
limited impacts across the remainder of coastal Mississippi.

Elsewhere across Southeast Louisiana and South Mississippi, little to
no impact is anticipated.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:

Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to check your emergency plan and emergency supplies
kit and take necessary actions to protect your family and secure your
home or business.

When making safety and preparedness decisions, do not focus on the
exact forecast track since hazards such as flooding rain, damaging
wind gusts, storm surge, and tornadoes extend well away from the
center of the storm.

If in a place that is vulnerable to high wind, such as near large
trees, a manufactured home, upper floors of a high-rise building, or
on a boat, plan to move to safe shelter.

If you live in a place particularly vulnerable to flooding, such as
near the ocean, in a low-lying or poor drainage area, plan to
move to safe shelter on higher ground.

When securing your property, outside preparations should be concluded
as soon as possible before conditions deteriorate. The onset of
strong gusty winds or flooding can cause certain preparedness
activities to become unsafe.

Be sure to let friends and family members know of your intentions for
weathering the storm and your whereabouts. Have someone located away
from the threatened area serve as your point of contact. Share vital
contact information with others. Keep cell phones handy and charged.

Check on those who may not be fully aware of the situation or who are
unable to make personal preparations.

If you are a visitor, know the name of the county or parish in which
you are located and where it is relative to current watches and
warnings. If staying at a hotel, ask the management staff about their
onsite disaster plan. Listen for evacuation orders, especially
pertaining to area visitors.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather Radio and local news
outlets for official storm information. Listen for possible changes
to the forecast.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in New Orleans LA around 11 PM CDT, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

properties.instruction:

the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

loose-fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early
morning or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat
exhaustion and heat stroke.

Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.description:
* LOCATIONS AFFECTED
- Yscloskey
- Delacroix
- Shell Beach

* WIND
- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Below tropical storm force wind
- Peak Wind Forecast: 25-35 mph with gusts to 55 mph

- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST
UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for wind 58
to 73 mph
- The wind threat has remained nearly steady from the
previous assessment.
- PLAN: Plan for dangerous wind of equivalent strong tropical
storm force.
- PREPARE: Efforts to protect life and property should now be
underway. Prepare for significant wind damage.
- ACT: Act now to complete preparations before the wind
becomes hazardous.

- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Significant
- Some damage to roofing and siding materials, along with
damage to porches, awnings, carports, and sheds. A few
buildings experiencing window, door, and garage door
failures. Mobile homes damaged, especially if unanchored.
Unsecured lightweight objects become dangerous projectiles.
- Several large trees snapped or uprooted, but with greater
numbers in places where trees are shallow rooted. Several
fences and roadway signs blown over.
- Some roads impassable from large debris, and more within
urban or heavily wooded places. A few bridges, causeways,
and access routes impassable.
- Scattered power and communications outages, but more
prevalent in areas with above ground lines.

* STORM SURGE
- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Life-threatening storm surge possible
- Peak Storm Surge Inundation: The potential for 3-5 feet
above ground somewhere within surge prone areas
- Window of concern: Friday morning until Saturday morning

- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST
UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for storm
surge flooding greater than 3 feet above ground
- The storm surge threat has remained nearly steady from the
previous assessment.
- PLAN: Plan for life-threatening storm surge flooding of
greater than 3 feet above ground.
- PREPARE: Storm surge flooding preparations should be
underway. Assemble disaster supplies and know your
evacuation route.
- ACT: Leave if evacuation orders are given for your area.
Failure to heed evacuation orders may result in the loss of
your life.

- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Significant
- Areas of inundation with storm surge flooding accentuated
by waves. Damage to several buildings, mainly near the
coast.
- Sections of some escape routes and secondary roads become
weakened or washed out, especially in usually vulnerable
low spots.
- Major marsh and shoreline erosion.
- Moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks, and piers.
Several small craft broken away from moorings, especially
in unprotected anchorages.

* FLOODING RAIN
- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST:
- Peak Rainfall Amounts: 1-3 inches, with locally higher
amounts

- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST
UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Little or no
potential for flooding rain

assessment.
- PLAN: There is little or no potential for flooding rain.
- PREPARE: Little to no preparations are needed to protect
against flooding rain at this time.
- ACT: Monitor for changes to the forecast.

- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Little to None

- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST:

UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Tornadoes not expected

your life.

by waves. Damage to several buildings, mainly near the
coast.

become weakened or washed out, especially in usually
vulnerable low spots.

and numerous rip currents.

assessment.

major flooding from heavy rain. Evacuations and rescues are
likely.

if you are in an area vulnerable to flooding.
- ACT: Heed any flood watches and warnings. Failure to take
action will likely result in serious injury or loss of life.

- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, and ditches may
become dangerous rivers. Flood control systems and barriers
may become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or
washed away. Many places where flood waters may cover
escape routes. Streets and parking lots become rivers of
moving water with underpasses submerged. Driving conditions
become dangerous. Many road and bridge closures with some
weakened or washed out.

* TORNADO
- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST:
- Situation is somewhat favorable for tornadoes

- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST
UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for a few
tornadoes
- The tornado threat has increased from the previous
assessment.
- PLAN: Emergency plans should include the potential for a
few tornadoes.
- PREPARE: If your shelter is particularly vulnerable to
tornadoes, prepare to relocate to safe shelter before
hazardous weather arrives.
- ACT: If a tornado warning is issued, be ready to shelter
quickly.

execution of emergency plans during tropical events.

power and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings,
chimneys toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or
overturned, large tree tops and branches snapped off,
shallow-rooted trees knocked over, moving vehicles blown
off roads, and small boats pulled from moorings.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to locally moderate coastal flooding with
elevated surf and dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 11 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and
harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is
likely. Isolated damage is possible in most vulnerable areas.
There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can
pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest risk of coastal flooding is
likely Sunday especially during the morning high tide.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 7 at 3:47PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Citrus and Levy
Counties.

.Elevated water levels continue on the Withlacoochee River at
Dunnellon due to excessive hydrilla growth along a 4.5 mile stretch
of river between U.S. 41 and Lake Rousseau. The hydrilla has been
acting like a dam and holding water back, keeping levels elevated.
With heavy rainfall occurring near Dunnellon, the river has continued
to rise and is forecast to remain in minor flood stage.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:45 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 28.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:45 PM EDT Wednesday was 28.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 28.6 feet
this evening.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.7
feet on 08/09/2003.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 400 AM EDT.

* WHAT...Up to 1.2 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Pablo Bay.

infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.

than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.0 ft above normal (6.78 ft MLLW) at 10:51 AM
Thursday 10/8, 1.0 ft above normal (6.86 ft MLLW) at 11:22 AM
Friday 10/9, 1.2 ft above normal (7.06 ft MLLW) at 11:50 AM
Saturday 10/10, 1.2 ft above normal (7.08 ft MLLW) at 12:18 PM
Sunday 10/11, 1.2 ft above normal (7.03 ft MLLW) at 12:46 PM
Monday 10/12, 1.1 ft above normal (6.90 ft MLLW) at 1:14 PM

surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued October 7 at 12:11PM MST until October 8 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions possible. Afternoon temperatures
102 to 106. Major Heat Risk.

* WHERE...In Arizona, Gila River Valley and Parker Valley. In
California, Chuckwalla Valley and Palo Verde Valley.

* WHEN...From 10 AM MST /10 AM PDT/ to 8 PM MST /8 PM PDT/ Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat
exhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat
stroke.
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued October 7 at 12:41PM MDT until October 9 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Boise ID
properties.description:
...FIRE WEATHER WATCH FOR DRY/WINDY WEATHER FRIDAY AFTERNOON...

.Dry and increasingly windy weather will develop Friday afternoon
in the Owyhee Mountains and Southern Highlands in Idaho ahead
of a cold front expected to pass through on Saturday. Concern is
greatest in the southern half of those zones.

The National Weather Service in Boise has issued a Fire Weather
Watch for winds and low relative humidities, which is in effect
Friday afternoon.

* AFFECTED AREA...In Idaho, Fire Weather Zones 423 Owyhee
Mountains and 426 Southern Highlands.

* TIMING...Friday afternoon.

* WINDS...West 15 to 20 mph with gusts up to 35 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...11 to 19 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...79 to 85 degrees.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are possible. Listen for later forecasts and possible Red Flag
Warnings.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 7 at 2:30PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM EDT Wednesday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to continue rising through minor
flood stage, reaching 2.9 feet late this week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 2.9
feet on 03/02/1998.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 230 AM EDT.

properties.description:
HLSTAE

This product covers eastern Florida panhandle, Florida Big Bend,
southeastern Alabama and southwestern Georgia

...NOAA HURRICANE HUNTERS FIND ISAIAS GATHERING STRENGTH...

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Hurricane Watch has been issued for Central Walton and North
Walton
- A Tropical Storm Watch has been issued for Holmes, Inland Bay,
Inland Gulf, and Washington

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Hurricane Watch is in effect for Central Walton and North
Walton
- A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for Holmes, Inland Bay,
Inland Gulf, and Washington
- A Storm Surge Watch and Hurricane Watch are in effect for
Coastal Bay, Coastal Gulf, and South Walton
- A Storm Surge Watch and Tropical Storm Watch are in effect for
Coastal Franklin, Coastal Jefferson, and Coastal Wakulla
- A Storm Surge Watch is in effect for Coastal Dixie and Coastal
Taylor

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 700 miles southwest of Panama City or about 720 miles
southwest of Apalachicola
- 22.6N 93.4W
- Storm Intensity 50 mph
- Movement East-northeast or 70 degrees at 8 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

...HURRICANE WATCH FOR WALTON COUNTY...
...TROPICAL STORM WATCHES FOR INLAND GULF AND BAY COUNTIES, AND
WASHINGTON AND HOLMES COUNTIES...

At 2 PM ET, Tropical Storm Isaias was still located in the Bay of
Campeche with maximum sustained winds of 50 mph and moving ENE at 8
mph. Isaias is forecast to turn northward in the next day or so and
accelerate in forward speed towards the central Gulf coast. Steady
strengthening is expected through much of the next couple of days,
although some weakening may be possible just before landfall. The wind
field is expected to expand considerably and may be lopsided towards
the east, leading to windier conditions for portions of our area. There
is still considerable uncertainty with both timing and track.
Conditions could begin to deteriorate across the Panhandle as early as
Friday morning.

Given the expected large size of Isaias, the wind threat may extend
well into the eastern portions of our area. An expected fast forward
speed may also lead to the wind threat extending further inland. Storm
surge will be possible along our whole coastline including the
Panhandle and Apalachee Bay. Inundation values of 5 to 7 feet above
ground level (AGL) are possible across the coastal Panhandle to Indian
Pass, 3 to 5 feet AGL from Indian Pass to the Aucilla River, and 2 to 4
feet AGL from the Aucilla River to Yankeetown.

Soggy conditions across the region from recent rainfall will make the
area more sensitive to flooding from additional heavy rainfall from
Isaias. Forecast rainfall totals of 3 to 6 inches is expected across
much of the area, with isolated amounts near 10 inches possible. If
realized, these values would likely cause at least isolated flash
flooding and some river flooding. It is too soon to determine exact
tornado impacts, if any, but a few cannot be ruled out at this time.


POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* FLOODING RAIN:
Prepare for life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible
extensive impacts across the FL Panhandle. Potential
impacts include:
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, and ditches may become
dangerous rivers. Flood control systems and barriers may become
stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.
Streets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with
underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.
Many road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.

Prepare for dangerous rainfall flooding having possible limited to
significant impacts across southeast Alabama, southwest Georgia, and
the Florida Big Bend.

* SURGE:
Prepare for life-threatening surge having possible extensive impacts
across the coastal Florida Panhandle and Florida Big Bend. Potential
impacts in this area include:
- Large areas of deep inundation with storm surge flooding
accentuated by battering waves. Structural damage to buildings,
with several washing away. Damage compounded by floating
debris. Locations may be uninhabitable for an extended period.
- Large sections of near-shore escape routes and secondary roads
washed out or severely flooded. Flood control systems and
barriers may become stressed.
- Severe beach erosion with significant dune loss.
- Major damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks, and piers. Many
small craft broken away from moorings, especially in
unprotected anchorages with some lifted onshore and stranded.

Elsewhere across eastern Florida panhandle, Florida Big Bend,
southeastern Alabama and southwestern Georgia, little to no impact is
anticipated.

* WIND:
Prepare for dangerous wind having possible significant impacts across
the Florida Panhandle. Potential impacts in this area include:
- Some damage to roofing and siding materials, along with damage
to porches, awnings, carports, and sheds. A few buildings
experiencing window, door, and garage door failures. Mobile
homes damaged, especially if unanchored. Unsecured lightweight
objects become dangerous projectiles.
- Several large trees snapped or uprooted, but with greater
numbers in places where trees are shallow rooted. Several
fences and roadway signs blown over.
- Some roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban
or heavily wooded places. A few bridges, causeways, and access
routes impassable.
- Scattered power and communications outages, but more prevalent
in areas with above ground lines.

Also, prepare for hazardous wind having possible limited impacts
across the Florida Big Bend and Southeast Alabama.

Elsewhere across eastern Florida panhandle, Florida Big Bend,
southeastern Alabama and southwestern Georgia, little to no impact is
anticipated.

* TORNADOES:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time
across eastern Florida panhandle, Florida Big Bend, southeastern
Alabama and southwestern Georgia.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to check your emergency plan and emergency supplies
kit and take necessary actions to protect your family and secure your
home or business.

When making safety and preparedness decisions, do not focus on the
exact forecast track since hazards such as flooding rain, damaging
wind gusts, storm surge, and tornadoes extend well away from the
center of the storm.

If you live in a place particularly vulnerable to flooding, such as
near the Gulf of America or a large inland lake, in a low-lying or
poor drainage area, or near an already swollen river, plan to move to
safe shelter on higher ground.

Always heed the advice of local officials and comply with orders that
are issued. Do not needlessly jeopardize your life or the lives of
others.

When securing your property, outside preparations should be concluded
as soon as possible before conditions deteriorate. The onset of
strong gusty winds or flooding can cause certain preparedness
activities to become unsafe.

Be sure to let friends and family members know of your intentions for
weathering the storm and your whereabouts. Have someone located away
from the threatened area serve as your point of contact. Share vital
contact information with others. Keep cell phones handy and charged.

Check on those who may not be fully aware of the situation or who are
unable to make personal preparations.

If you are a visitor, know the name of the county in which you are
located and where it is relative to current watches and warnings. If
staying at a hotel, ask the management staff about their onsite
disaster plan. Listen for evacuation orders, especially pertaining to
area visitors.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather Radio and local news
outlets for official storm information. Listen for possible changes
to the forecast.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

properties.description:
HLSLIX

This product covers Southeast Louisiana and South Mississippi

...HURRICANE WATCHES EXPANDED INLAND IN COASTAL MISSISSIPPI...


NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Hurricane Watch has been issued for Northern Harrison and
Northern Jackson

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Hurricane Watch is in effect for Northern Harrison and
Northern Jackson
- A Storm Surge Watch and Hurricane Watch are in effect for
Southern Harrison and Southern Jackson
- A Storm Surge Watch and Tropical Storm Watch are in effect for
Eastern Orleans, Lower Plaquemines, Lower St. Bernard,
Southeast St. Tammany, and Southern Hancock
- A Storm Surge Watch is in effect for Upper St. Bernard

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 540 miles south-southwest of New Orleans LA or about 600
miles south-southwest of Gulfport MS
- 22.6N 93.4W
- Storm Intensity 50 mph
- Movement East-northeast or 70 degrees at 8 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Isaias is currently in the southwest Gulf and will
continue to strengthen as it moves to the east-northeast and
eventually the northeast through Friday. Tropical Storm Isaias is
forecast to bring the threat of tropical storm force wind gusts,
locally heavy rainfall, and storm surge of 3 to 5 feet to coastal
portions of southeast Louisiana from the mouth of the Mississippi
River to the Rigolets and from Bay Saint Louis westward in coastal
Mississippi. Isaias is forecast to bring the threat of hurricane force
wind gusts, locally heavy rainfall, and storm surge of 5 to 7 feet
from Bay Saint Louis eastward in coastal Mississippi. The most likely
time for impacts will be Friday into Saturday.

Storm surge watches have been issued from the mouth of the Mississippi
River to the Alabama and Mississippi state line. Hurricane watches are
in effect from Ocean Springs to the Alabama and Mississippi state
line. Tropical storm watches are in effect from the Jefferson and
Plaquemine Parish line in southeast Louisiana to Ocean Springs in
coastal Mississippi.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Prepare for life-threatening wind having possible extensive impacts
for locations east of Ocean Springs in coastal Mississippi. Potential
impacts in this area include:
- Considerable roof damage to sturdy buildings, with some having
window, door, and garage door failures leading to structural
damage. Mobile homes severely damaged, with some destroyed.
Damage accentuated by airborne projectiles. Locations may be
uninhabitable for weeks.
- Many large trees snapped or uprooted along with fences and
roadway signs blown over.
- Some roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban
or heavily wooded places. Several bridges, causeways, and
access routes impassable.
- Large areas with power and communications outages.

Also, prepare for dangerous wind having possible limited to
significant impacts for locations west of Ocean Springs in coastal
Mississippi and for extreme coastal portions of southeast Louisiana
from the mouth of the Mississippi River eastward.

* SURGE:
Prepare for life-threatening surge having possible extensive impacts
for coastal locations east of Ocean Springs in coastal Mississippi.
Potential impacts in this area include:
- Large areas of deep inundation with storm surge flooding
accentuated by battering waves. Structural damage to buildings,
with several washing away. Damage compounded by floating
debris. Locations may be uninhabitable for an extended period.
- Large sections of near-shore escape routes and secondary roads
washed out or severely flooded. Flood control systems and
barriers may become stressed.
- Severe beach erosion with significant dune loss.
- Major damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks, and piers. Many
small craft broken away from moorings, especially in
unprotected anchorages with some lifted onshore and stranded.

Also, prepare for locally hazardous surge having possible significant
impacts for coastal locations west of Ocean Springs in coastal
Mississippi and for locations outside of the hurricane risk reduction
system in southeast Louisiana from the Pearl River south to the mouth
of the Mississippi.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Prepare for life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible
extensive impacts for locations in Jackson County in coastal
Mississippi. Potential impacts include:
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may
become dangerous rivers. Flood control systems and barriers may
become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.
Streets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with
underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.
Many road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.

Prepare for dangerous rainfall flooding having possible limited to
significant impacts for the rest of coastal Mississippi.

* TORNADOES:
Prepare for a tornado event having possible limited impacts across
coastal Mississippi. Potential impacts include:
- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power
and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys
toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats
pulled from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southeast Louisiana and South Mississippi, little to
no impact is anticipated.

AQAPSR

The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ) has issued an
Ozone High Pollution Advisory for the Phoenix Metro Area on Wednesday.

This means that forecast weather conditions combined with existing
ozone levels are expected to result in local maximum 8-hour ozone
concentrations that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects
increase as air quality deteriorates.

Ozone is an air contaminant which can cause breathing difficulties
for children, older adults, as well as persons with respiratory
problems. A decrease in physical activity is recommended.

You are urged to car pool, telecommute or use mass transit.
The use of gasoline-powered equipment should be reduced or done late
in the day.

For details on this High Pollution Advisory, visit the ADEQ internet
site at www.azdeq.gov/forecast/phoenix or call 602-771-2300.

properties.description:
HLSMOB

This product covers portions of southwest Alabama...northwest Florida...south
central Alabama...and inland southeast Mississippi.

**HURRICANE AND STORM SURGE WATCHES ISSUED FOR PORTIONS OF THE
NORTHERN GULF COAST FOR STRENGTHENING ISAIAS**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Storm Surge Watch and Hurricane Watch have been issued for
Baldwin Central, Baldwin Coastal, Escambia Coastal, Mobile
Central, Mobile Coastal, Okaloosa Coastal, and Santa Rosa
Coastal
- A Hurricane Watch has been issued for Baldwin Inland, Escambia
Inland, Mobile Inland, Okaloosa Inland, and Santa Rosa Inland

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Storm Surge Watch and Hurricane Watch are in effect for
Baldwin Central, Baldwin Coastal, Escambia Coastal, Mobile
Central, Mobile Coastal, Okaloosa Coastal, and Santa Rosa
Coastal
- A Hurricane Watch is in effect for Baldwin Inland, Escambia
Inland, Mobile Inland, Okaloosa Inland, and Santa Rosa Inland

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 660 miles south-southwest of Mobile AL or about 680 miles
southwest of Pensacola FL
- 22.4N 93.6W
- Storm Intensity 45 mph
- Movement East-northeast or 70 degrees at 8 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Isaias continues to organize across the southwestern
Gulf and is expected to strengthen through through Friday morning.
Isaias is currently moving east-northeast and should eventually turn
northward and accelerate towards the north central Gulf coast. As it
nears the coast, wind fields will expand with the potential for
significant wind impacts and a life threatening storm surge along and
to the east of where the hurricane makes landfall. There still remains
uncertainty with the eventual speed and track of the hurricane so
everyone should continue to closely monitor the latest forecast over
the next few days.

Areas of heavy rainfall and flooding are possible although with the
fast speed of the hurricane at landfall we are currently expecting 3 to
6 inches with localized amounts up to 10 inches near the coast. In
addition, a favorable environment for tornadoes will also develop to
the east of the track as it moves inland Friday through Saturday.

Please continue to monitor the latest forecast updates and follow the
advise of your local emergency management officials.


POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* SURGE:
Prepare for life-threatening surge having possible extensive impacts
across the Alabama and western Florida panhandle coasts. Potential
impacts in this area include:
- Large areas of deep inundation with storm surge flooding
accentuated by battering waves. Structural damage to buildings,
with several washing away. Damage compounded by floating
debris. Locations may be uninhabitable for an extended period.
- Large sections of near-shore escape routes and secondary roads
washed out or severely flooded. Flood control systems and
barriers may become stressed.
- Severe beach erosion with significant dune loss.
- Major damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks, and piers. Many
small craft broken away from moorings, especially in
unprotected anchorages with some lifted onshore and stranded.

Elsewhere across portions of southwest Alabama...northwest
Florida...south central Alabama...and inland southeast Mississippi.,
little to no impact is anticipated.

* WIND:
Prepare for life-threatening wind having possible extensive impacts
across coastal Alabama and the western Florida panhandle. Potential
impacts in this area include:
- Considerable roof damage to sturdy buildings, with some having
window, door, and garage door failures leading to structural
damage. Mobile homes severely damaged, with some destroyed.
Damage accentuated by airborne projectiles. Locations may be
uninhabitable for weeks.
- Many large trees snapped or uprooted along with fences and
roadway signs blown over.
- Some roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban
or heavily wooded places.
- Large areas with power and communications outages.

Also, prepare for dangerous wind having possible limited to
significant impacts across interior portions of southwest and south
central Alabama.

* TORNADOES:
Prepare for a tornado event having possible limited impacts across
coastal southwest Alabama, the western Florida panhandle, and portions
of southwest and south central Alabama. Potential impacts include:
- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power
and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys
toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats
pulled from moorings.

Elsewhere across portions of southwest Alabama...northwest
Florida...south central Alabama...and inland southeast Mississippi.,
little to no impact is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Prepare for life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible
extensive impacts across coastal Alabama and the western Florida
panhandle. Potential impacts include:
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may
become dangerous rivers. Flood control systems and barriers may
become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.
Streets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with
underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.
Many road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.

Prepare for dangerous rainfall flooding having possible significant
impacts across interior areas of southwest and south central Alabama.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to check your emergency plan and emergency supplies
kit and take necessary actions to protect your family and secure your
home or business.

When making safety and preparedness decisions, do not focus on the
exact forecast track since hazards such as flooding rain, damaging
wind gusts, storm surge, and tornadoes extend well away from the
center of the storm.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For the latest detailed evacuation and shelter information...please
refer to your local emergency management agency at the phone number
or website listed below.
- Coastal Alabama:
- Baldwin County: 251-972-6807 or
www.baldwincountyal.gov/departments/EMA
- Mobile County: 251-460-8000 or mobilecountyema.gov
- Northwest Florida:
- Escambia County: 850-471-6400 or myescambia.com/beready
- Santa Rosa County: 850-983-5360 www.santarosa.fl.gov/emergency
- Okaloosa County: 850-651-7150 or myokaloosa.com/emergency-management
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Mobile AL around 5 PM CDT, or sooner if conditions warrant.

HLSLIX

This product covers Southeast Louisiana and South Mississippi

...HURRICANE AND STORM SURGE WATCHES ISSUED FOR PORTIONS OF THE
AREA FOR STRENGTHENING ISAIAS...


NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Storm Surge Watch and Hurricane Watch have been issued for
Southern Harrison and Southern Jackson
- A Storm Surge Watch and Tropical Storm Watch have been issued
for Eastern Orleans, Lower Plaquemines, Lower St. Bernard,
Southeast St. Tammany, and Southern Hancock
- A Storm Surge Watch has been issued for Upper St. Bernard

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Storm Surge Watch and Hurricane Watch are in effect for
Southern Harrison and Southern Jackson
- A Storm Surge Watch and Tropical Storm Watch are in effect for
Eastern Orleans, Lower Plaquemines, Lower St. Bernard,
Southeast St. Tammany, and Southern Hancock
- A Storm Surge Watch is in effect for Upper St. Bernard

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 560 miles south-southwest of New Orleans LA or about 620
miles south-southwest of Gulfport MS
- 22.4N 93.6W
- Storm Intensity 45 mph
- Movement East-northeast or 70 degrees at 8 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Isaias is currently in the southwest Gulf and will
continue to strengthen as it moves to the east-northeast and
eventually the northeast through Friday. Tropical Storm Isaias is
forecast to bring the threat of tropical storm force wind gusts,
locally heavy rainfall, and storm surge of 3 to 5 feet to coastal
portions of southeast Louisiana from the mouth of the Mississippi
River to the Rigolets and from Bay Saint Louis westward in coastal
Mississippi. Isaias is forecast to bring the threat of hurricane force
wind gusts, locally heavy rainfall, and storm surge of 5 to 7 feet
from Bay Saint Louis eastward in coastal Mississippi. The most likely
time for impacts will be Friday into Saturday.

Storm surge watches have been issued from the mouth of the Mississippi
River to the Alabama and Mississippi state line. Hurricane watches are
in effect from Ocean Springs to the Alabama and Mississippi state
line. Tropical storm watches are in effect from the Jefferson and
Plaquemine Parish line in southeast Louisiana to Ocean Springs in
coastal Mississippi.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Prepare for life-threatening wind having possible extensive impacts
for locations east of Ocean Springs in coastal Mississippi.
Potential impacts in this area include:
- Considerable roof damage to sturdy buildings, with some having
window, door, and garage door failures leading to structural
damage. Mobile homes severely damaged, with some destroyed.
Damage accentuated by airborne projectiles. Locations may be
uninhabitable for weeks.
- Many large trees snapped or uprooted along with fences and
roadway signs blown over.
- Some roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban
or heavily wooded places. Several bridges, causeways, and
access routes impassable.
- Large areas with power and communications outages.

Also, prepare for dangerous wind having possible limited to
significant impacts for locations west of Ocean Springs in coastal
Mississippi and for extreme coastal portions of southeast Louisiana
from the mouth of the Mississippi River eastward.

Elsewhere across Southeast Louisiana and South Mississippi, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* SURGE:
Prepare for life-threatening surge having possible extensive impacts
for coastal locations east of Ocean Springs in coastal Mississippi. Potential
impacts in this area include:
- Large areas of deep inundation with storm surge flooding
accentuated by battering waves. Structural damage to buildings,
with several washing away. Damage compounded by floating
debris. Locations may be uninhabitable for an extended period.
- Large sections of near-shore escape routes and secondary roads
washed out or severely flooded. Flood control systems and
barriers may become stressed.
- Severe beach erosion with significant dune loss.
- Major damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks, and piers. Many
small craft broken away from moorings, especially in
unprotected anchorages with some lifted onshore and stranded.

Also, prepare for locally hazardous surge having possible significant
impacts for coastal locations west of Ocean Springs in coastal Mississippi
and for locations outside of the hurricane risk reduction system in southeast
Louisiana from the Pearl River south to the mouth of the Mississippi.

Elsewhere across Southeast Louisiana and South Mississippi, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Prepare for life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible
extensive impacts for locations in Jackson County in coastal Mississippi.
Potential impacts include:
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may
become dangerous rivers. Flood control systems and barriers may
become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.
Streets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with
underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.
Many road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.

Prepare for dangerous rainfall flooding having possible limited to
significant impacts for the rest of coastal Mississippi.

Elsewhere across Southeast Louisiana and South Mississippi, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* TORNADOES:
Prepare for a tornado event having possible limited impacts across coastal
Mississippi. Potential impacts include:
- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power
and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys
toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats
pulled from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southeast Louisiana and South Mississippi, little to
no impact is anticipated.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to check your emergency plan and emergency supplies
kit and take necessary actions to protect your family and secure your
home or business.

When making safety and preparedness decisions, do not focus on the
exact forecast track since hazards such as flooding rain, damaging
wind gusts, storm surge, and tornadoes extend well away from the
center of the storm.

If in a place that is vulnerable to high wind, such as near large
trees, a manufactured home, upper floors of a high-rise building, or
on a boat, plan to move to safe shelter.

If you live in a place particularly vulnerable to flooding, such as
near the ocean, in a low-lying or poor drainage area, plan to
move to safe shelter on higher ground.

When securing your property, outside preparations should be concluded
as soon as possible before conditions deteriorate. The onset of
strong gusty winds or flooding can cause certain preparedness
activities to become unsafe.

Be sure to let friends and family members know of your intentions for
weathering the storm and your whereabouts. Have someone located away
from the threatened area serve as your point of contact. Share vital
contact information with others. Keep cell phones handy and charged.

Check on those who may not be fully aware of the situation or who are
unable to make personal preparations.

If you are a visitor, know the name of the county or parish in which
you are located and where it is relative to current watches and
warnings. If staying at a hotel, ask the management staff about their
onsite disaster plan. Listen for evacuation orders, especially
pertaining to area visitors.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather Radio and local news
outlets for official storm information. Listen for possible changes
to the forecast.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

-----------

Service in New Orleans LA around 5 PM CDT, or sooner if conditions
warrant.
